chapters.1: Paul greets the church at Colosse and thanks God for their faith and love, which he heard about from Epaphras. He prays they'll grow in wisdom and understanding, then launches into a powerful description of who Christ is: the image of the invisible God, creator and sustainer of everything, and head of the church. Paul explains that through Christ's death God reconciled all things to himself, and that Paul's own suffering and ministry serve to make this message known to the Gentiles.
chapters.2: Paul warns the Colossians not to be talked out of their faith by clever-sounding philosophy or man-made religious rules, because everything they need is found in Christ, in whom the fullness of God dwells. He reminds them that through faith and baptism they died and rose with Christ, and their sins were forgiven. He tells them not to let anyone bind them with legalistic rules about food, festivals, or self-made humility, since those are just shadows, not the substance that is found in Christ.
chapters.3: Because believers have been raised with Christ, Paul tells them to set their minds on heavenly things and put to death sinful habits like anger, lying, and greed, replacing them with compassion, kindness, humility, and forgiveness, all held together by love. He urges them to let Christ's peace and word rule their hearts and worship, doing everything for the Lord's glory. He then gives household instructions for wives, husbands, children, and servants to live out their faith in ordinary relationships.
chapters.4: Paul closes with instructions for masters to treat servants fairly and for everyone to keep praying and to speak with grace to outsiders. He sends personal greetings from co-workers like Tychicus, Onesimus, Mark, and Luke, and mentions Epaphras's prayers for the Colossians. He asks that the letter be shared with the church at Laodicea and gives a final personal word to Archippus before signing off.
